# ReShiki 0.11.0

This release promotes the tested October 5 nightly application code, with the version and release documentation updated and two small corrections to the reference-test pipeline. The ongoing refactoring branches are excluded.

- Interactive Rust **MMFF94, MMFF94s and UFF** optimization, atom dragging and pinning, and editable 3D projections. **Cmd/Ctrl+Shift+D** opens optimization.
- Mouse and keyboard drawing work together by default, with atom keys, bond/ring shortcuts, arrow navigation and marked ring closure. **F8** toggles keyboard drawing.
- Persistent atom and bond highlights, independent contracted-label styles, precise transforms and stable selection rotation.
- Supported embedded ChemDraw objects copied from Windows Office paste as editable atoms and bonds.
- Ordinary Copy prepares molecular text or ChemDoodle reaction data for the editor's text-field **Load** workflow. Built-in templates follow the active journal size.
- Reduced temporary memory use, safer template saves, and preserved reaction membership when joining fragments.

The installed application remains one executable and works without Python or RDKit. Geometry optimization explores local conformations; it does not guarantee a global minimum. Difficult sampling can fall back to one conformer. Floating secondary double-bond strokes in some projected C60 views remain unresolved.

**Drawing compatibility:** older drawings remain readable. Files saved by 0.11 use document format 19 and cannot open in 0.10.0 or earlier. Keep a separate copy when testing.

macOS downloads are signed and notarized. Windows and Linux downloads remain unsigned; Windows signing is pending. The optional Microsoft 365 add-in remains an MVP for sideloaded testing, and its real-host acceptance is pending.

[Complete changes and contributor credits](https://reshiki.com/developer/changes-0.11/) · [3D and keyboard drawing](https://reshiki.com/developer/3d-keyboard-drawing/) · [ChemDoodle handoff](https://reshiki.com/developer/scifinder-handoff/).
